The problem presents a system of 35 logical constraints (Clauses) governing the casting of spells by three wizards across three stages. The provided formal SAT information includes a Z3 solver output labeled as "UNSAT core" and a specific `<unsat_core_clauses>` section.

Clause 32 states $P \lor Q$.
Clause 33 states $\neg P \lor \neg Q$.
By logical deduction, $P \lor Q$ and $\neg P \lor \neg Q$ are mutually exclusive; they cannot both be true simultaneously in any consistent assignment. If $P$ is true, $\neg P$ is false, forcing $Q$ to be true. If $Q$ is true, $\neg Q$ is false, forcing $P$ to be true. However, if either $P$ or $Q$ is false, the respective disjunctive clause fails, while the other might fail if the other variable is also false. More formally, the conjunction $(P \lor Q) \land (\neg P \lor \neg Q)$ simplifies to $(P \land \neg P) \lor (Q \land \neg Q) \lor (\neg P \land Q) \lor (P \land \neg Q)$, which reduces to False.

Since the set of constraints includes this contradiction, the entire system is unsatisfiable. The Z3 certificate confirms this by returning `true` for the unsat core (implying the clauses listed form the core unsatisfiability) and explicitly labeling the result as `UNSAT`.

**Answer:**
